Fig. 2. Overview of our pipeline for UI generation, illustrated through a factory-style production line metaphor. From a user input, the system performs requirement analysis to extract Base UI-DSL bricks, each embedding provenance for traceability. These bricks then progress along the conveyor through the Layout, Interaction, Relation, and Style Stage Generations, where robotic arms illustrate AI Inference and workers symbolize User Feedback operations such as accept, reject, add custom, which users can apply at any stage of the pipeline. The evolving DSL can be rendered into UI outputs at any point, producing successive versions (Version 1, Version 2, . . . , X).

Fig. 8. P4’s staged workflow across requirement analysis, layout, interaction, relation, and style stages. The figure shows both AI inferences (green) and user interventions (purple), including rejections of intent and global specifications, as well as additions to relation and style specifications.

Fig. 5. User preference results across prompts. (a–c) show best-choice and second-choice votes for Dashboard, Productivity, and Portfolio prompts respectively. (d) summarizes overall rankings aggregated across all prompts.

Fig. 9. P4’s UI generation and subsequent refinement. After the first UI draft was generated, the participant added new component and relation specifications (A, B) and then regenerated the interface, resulting in a revised UI that better matched their intentions.
